name: Ambiguity Tolerance Profiling
description: Measures the text's acceptance of semantic and contextual ambiguity without forceful resolution
mechanism: This method evaluates how a text handles unresolved concepts or double meanings. Due to rigorous RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) models aimed at clarity and harmlessness, large language models are heavily penalized during training for leaving concepts ambiguous. Consequently, when faced with an ambiguous topic, an LLM will forcefully 'resolve' it by either explicitly listing out all possible interpretations ('On one hand... on the other hand') or defaulting to a neutral, overly-explained stance. Authentic human writing naturally tolerates high degrees of ambiguity, leaving statements open to contextual interpretation without feeling the need to mathematically balance every perspective.
parameters:
Analysis type: Pragmatic discourse analysis
Media: Text
Input: Raw text string
Minimum length: 150 words
Output: Ambiguity tolerance score (0-100)
Processing: Semantic dependency and discourse mapping
accuracy: High — 75-88%. Exceptionally effective at distinguishing nuanced human philosophy, literature, and opinion pieces from AI-generated equivalents.
source: Pragmatic linguistics and LLM alignment behavior research.
useCase: Detecting text generated by overly-aligned AI models that exhibit an obsessive need to clarify, disambiguate, and neutrally balance every statement.
strengths:
• Targets the fundamental psychological alignment of LLMs rather than simple vocabulary
• Very effective on argumentative and philosophical texts
• Hard to evade via simple prompting
limitations:
• May flag highly structured human academic papers that strictly define all terms
• Requires deep semantic parsing, which is computationally expensive

references.title: Jawahar, G. et al. (2020). Automatic Detection of Machine Generated Text: A Critical Survey. COLING.
